newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's Peters said 1998 tax cuts never in question.
newsitem.headline: NZ's Peters said 1998 tax cuts never in question.

text.p: Treasurer Winston Peters told Radio New Zealand on Tuesday that the three percent tax cuts planned for July 1998 have never been in question.

He was commenting on Radio New Zealand on comments from senior cabinet minister Jenny Shipley who on Monday accused Peters and Prime Minister Jim Bolger of "political michief-making" for suggesting future tax cuts might not go ahead if the comulsory pension scheme lost the September referendum.
"The 3 percent tax cuts as at July 1 next year are legislated for and they have never been in question," Peters said.

"The second and third and fourth tax cuts that we are talking about, that is the two percent, then one, one and one, were in the Coalition Agreement because I put them there, not because of the National Party, but because New Zealand First wanted them in there as part of a long-term retirement savings scheme," he said.
Peters said the later tax cuts were put there to help persuade people to enter into a long-term retirement scheme.
"So any mischief-making does not come from our quarter."
He said the later tax cuts were always linked to the compulsory pension scheme.
Peters noted Shipley and Finance Minister Bill Birch were part of the design of the compulsory scheme.

Peters said in a statement that Shipley was correct saying there could be on-going tax cuts with the present pension scheme "but this will mean substantial reductions to the current payout, a further lift in the retirement age or increased public
debt, or a mixture of all three".
